name: colliery-brass-band
style: Instrumental. A northern colliery brass band is rehearsing in the function room next door, and we hear it through the wall of a busy local pub on quiz night. Only the low end comes through clearly: E-flat and B-flat basses and baritone horns walking a lazy, good-humoured oompah figure, a soft bass drum on every downbeat. A cornet is somewhere behind the plaster, muffled and distant, playing short held tones and never a tune. The room around us is warm and close: glasses, chair legs, a low indistinct murmur with no words. Lo-fi, boxy, dull top end, lots of space in the middle for people talking over it. Near the end the band drops out until there is a single long tuba note and rain on the window. Then, for the last two seconds, the full band bursts in with one bright, cheeky rising fanfare stab and stops dead.
exclude: vocals, singing, spoken words, crowd chanting, orchestral strings, epic trailer brass, cinematic hybrid, synth brass, piano lead

name: rhythm-section-trio
style: Instrumental corner-of-the-bar jazz trio, 112 BPM, swung eighths, 4/4, F major. Upright double bass walking steady quarter notes. Snare played with brushes only, slow circular swirls, soft feathered hi-hat on 2 and 4. Vibraphone gives just two-note stabs, short and dry, one every two bars, motor off. Mixed low and distant, bass forward, wide gaps in the midrange, small wooden room. Around 0:28 the brushes drop out and the bass walks downward alone, half time, under light rain against glass. At 0:35 vibraphone climbs one quick four-note arpeggio, a single small bell rings, hard stop.
exclude: vocals, scat, singing, saxophone, trumpet lead, piano melody, smooth jazz, crowd chant, drum solo

name: squeezebox-folk-session
style: instrumental English pub folk session recorded live in a small back room, close and boozy. A two-row melodeon works its left-hand bass buttons in a steady oom-pah push and pull, a frame drum (bodhran) keeps a loose tipper beat, a battered steel-string acoustic strums open chords; players slightly behind the beat, glasses clink, chairs creak, a low warm room murmur with no words. Rhythmic and chordal only, no tune on top, mids kept clear for speech. Mid-way the whole room drops out to a hush: one held melodeon chord breathing slowly over rain on a window. Final seconds: the squeezebox kicks back in with a cheeky quick run of chords and the piece ends on a single brass bell clang
exclude: vocals, singing, sing-along, crowd chant, spoken words, fiddle lead, tin whistle lead, celtic epic, irish pub chorus, uilleann pipes, sad piano, cinematic strings
